subject: Privacy & Digital Rights
title: The NSA's Global Reach
description: A short lesson to help you apply The NSA's Global Reach.

hook.text: The NSA can intercept phone calls, emails, and texts from almost anyone on Earth. Legally.

buildup.text: Created in 1952, the NSA grew into the largest intelligence agency, with a budget exceeding $10 billion.

discovery.text: Snowden revealed programs that collected metadata on millions of Americans' phone calls daily.

twist.text: The NSA argued it only collected 'metadata' — who you called, when, how long. Not the content.

climax.text: But metadata reveals patterns: your doctor, your lawyer, your lover. It tells a story without words.

punchline.text: They don't read your calls. They don't need to.

quiz.question: Why is metadata collection considered a privacy concern?
options: It reveals patterns like who you contact and when
It includes the full text of every message
It only applies to international calls
